top_defects: Transient prod 'Server error' on the very first screen_unified call (case 1) — succeeded on identical retry ~4.3s (cold blip, not a schema/logic defect).

find_gics 400/empty on multi-word phrasing with a slash ('technology / information technology sector') — bare word 'information technology' resolved cleanly to '45'. Minor resolver brittleness on punctuated queries.

No direct `inventory_turnover` ratio concept exists; inventory efficiency must be expressed via `dio` (Days Inventory Outstanding, the inverse). Correct answer WAS in find_fsconcept top-k, so not a blocking gap — but a named turnover ratio would be more obvious to a dumb client.

cases.question: Quality at a reasonable price: net margin above its own sector's average, revenue up every year for 3 years, and P/E below 25.
tool_calls: screen_unified(fundamental=[net_margin/above_average vs_cohort{own:true}, revenue/consecutive_growth N=3, pe/below thr=25], asset_type=[Common Stock])
cases.evidence_check: net_margin.cohort_benchmark shown with cohort_scope=own_sector (GOOG 0.548 vs sector 0.215); revenue growth series[] with years_checked=3, window=min_yoy; pe level all <25.
cases.confusion_note: Obvious once schema read. 'each vs its own sector' correctly = vs_cohort{own:true} per schema. First call hit a transient Server error; identical retry succeeded.
cases.reason: All three legs evidenced; per-stock cohort benchmark shown; every P/E strictly <25 and net_margin > own-sector benchmark.

defects.desc: Transient Server error on first attempt, fine on retry

cases.question: Asset-light compounders: capex under 5% of revenue AND revenue compounding over 15% a year over 3 years.
tool_calls: screen_unified(fundamental=[capex lower_than revenue multiple=0.05 (relation), revenue/compound_growth thr=0.15 N=3])
cases.result_summary: count=32. NVDA(capex 2.8% rev, 3y CAGR ~100%), AVGO(1.0%, 24%), ASML(5.0%).
cases.evidence_check: Relation shows value_a (capex, stored NEGATIVE outflow) + value_b (revenue) + ratio (0.028); _conventions explains the sign. revenue growth window=3y_cagr, value>0.15.
cases.confusion_note: capex<5%-of-revenue is a RELATION not a level — schema's 'percent-of is a FRACTION' guidance made multiple=0.05 obvious. Sign of capex handled by server (ratio positive).
cases.reason: Both operands + ratio shown with correct outflow-sign handling; all ratios <0.05 and CAGR >15%.

cases.question: Banks with ROE above the banking-sector average and dividend yield over 4%.
cases.result_summary: count=32. All banks (Agri Bank China, CMB, Intesa, BNP, ING, NatWest...).
cases.evidence_check: roe.cohort_benchmark=0.0884 (banking avg), cohort_scope=candidate_universe (=the banks scope); each roe > benchmark; dividend_yield all >0.04.
cases.confusion_note: Schema explicitly says scope universe to the sector and OMIT vs_cohort so 'above average' means above the sector avg automatically — did exactly that. Clean.
cases.reason: Sector resolved + scoped; benchmark is the banking-sector average; every hit above it and >4% yield.

cases.question: Companies with over $5 billion of revenue AND net profit margin over 20%. (absolute USD, cross-market)
cases.result_summary: count=32. NVDA, AAPL, GOOG, MSFT, TSMC(TW), Samsung(KO)...
cases.evidence_check: revenue.value carries unit='usd' (466bn AAPL, 271bn Samsung) — absolute USD, cross-market (US/TW/KO); net_margin all >=0.20 (Samsung 0.2146 borderline-correct).
cases.confusion_note: Was the absolute-$ revenue an 'above' level or a size knob? Schema reserves min/max_market_cap for CAP; revenue-$ correctly goes as concept=revenue + above + threshold in USD. unit:usd confirms server USD-normalized it.
cases.reason: Absolute-USD revenue threshold honored cross-market; margin filter correct.

cases.question: Dividend stalwarts: paid a dividend every year for the last 10 years and never cut it. (10-year window — mind data depth)
cases.evidence_check: notes[] state: 'the data exists, but NO company has 10 years of annual history (deepest ~5y) — a 0 count here is INSUFFICIENT HISTORY, not nobody qualified. Re-ask with N<=5.'
cases.confusion_note: None. This is the depth trap and the tool handled it exactly right — a guided note, not a bare 0.
cases.reason: N=10 exceeds ~4-5y data depth; server returns a clear INSUFFICIENT-HISTORY note per metric with a re-ask suggestion.

cases.question: Cheap but not junk: P/E between 5 and 12 with positive free cash flow.
cases.result_summary: count=32. China banks (pe 7.6-8.4), Shell, Novo Nordisk, TotalEnergies, AT&T — all pe 5-12.
cases.evidence_check: pe.value all within [5,12] (min 7.59, max 11.26 — no sub-2 junk); free_cash_flow.value all positive (usd).
cases.reason: Both bounds of the band respected, no sub-2 junk P/E, FCF strictly positive.

cases.question: Operating-leverage plays: earnings growing faster than revenue over the last 3 years.
cases.result_summary: count=32. NVDA(NI cagr 2.02 vs rev 1.00), GOOG(0.30 vs 0.13), META(0.38 vs 0.20)...
cases.evidence_check: Relation shows BOTH cagr_a (earnings) and cagr_b (revenue), window=cagr_3y; cagr_a > cagr_b in every row.
cases.confusion_note: None; growth_faster_than takes no threshold (schema says the growth relations take none). N=3 from 'last 3 years'.
cases.reason: Both CAGRs shown; earnings CAGR exceeds revenue CAGR everywhere over 3y.

cases.question: The most financially volatile US technology companies. (volatility + sector + country)
cases.result_summary: count=32. CRM(yoy_std 5.57), NVDA(2.78), ZM, NOW, IBM, AVGO — sorted desc.
cases.evidence_check: net_income.value = yoy_std (dispersion), years_checked=3; all US IT-sector names; sorted most-volatile first.
cases.confusion_note: 'financially volatile' is fuzzy (price vol vs earnings vol). Chose earnings volatility via the curated `volatile` pattern (yoy_std) — grounded, evidenced. A reasonable read, not a guess.
cases.reason: Volatility + sector(45) + country(US) all applied; earnings-dispersion evidence shown and sorted.

defects.desc: 'financially volatile' is ambiguous; interpreted as earnings volatility (could also mean price/FCF volatility)

cases.question: Companies that spend roughly a quarter of their revenue on R&D.
cases.result_summary: count=32. AMD(0.234), INTC(0.261), MRK(0.243), AZN, MediaTek, MRVL(0.253)...
cases.evidence_check: Relation shows value_a(rnd)+value_b(revenue)+ratio; all ratios within default +-10% band of 0.25 (0.230-0.261).
cases.confusion_note: 'roughly a quarter' -> ratio_near target=0.25 with default band; schema's 'percent-of is a FRACTION' made 0.25 obvious.
cases.reason: All hits sit within +-10% of 25% R&D-to-revenue with both operands + ratio shown; R&D-heavy semis/pharma as expected.

cases.question: Companies with improving inventory efficiency. (may not be a screenable concept)
tool_calls: find_fsconcept(inventory turnover) -> dio (Days Inventory Outstanding) surfaced; no direct inventory_turnover ratio
cases.result_summary: count=24. MSFT, AMZN, TSMC, TSLA, WMT, COST — DIO falling every year.
cases.evidence_check: dio.series[] all-negative each year (DIO shrinking = inventory clears faster = improving efficiency), years_checked=3.
cases.confusion_note: There is no named `inventory_turnover` ratio concept, so 'efficiency improving' was mapped to the inverse `dio` DECLINING. dio was in find_fsconcept top-k, so the right answer was reachable without a low-confidence back-off.
cases.reason: Concept turned out screenable via DIO (the standard inverse) declining; evidence (falling series) is coherent, retailers dominate as expected.

defects.desc: No direct inventory-turnover ratio concept; must be expressed as DIO declining (correct but less obvious for a naive client)
